subject: BeaconForge & Synture — integration validation matrix and edge-case runbook
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@beaconforge.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: integration-team@beaconforge.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: BeaconForge / Synture — initial validation scope and runtime spec

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for taking this on. As discussed in the call, BeaconForge is working with Synture to certify a joint connector that will call Redwood's hosted and private runtimes for our summarization + extraction flow. We need a partner-led validation pass focused on:

- end-to-end correctness (model parity between hosted and private)
- latency & tail behavior under simulated burst loads
- tokenization/encoding edge cases (non-UTF8 payloads, long prompts, multi-lingual inputs)
- KV-cache/streaming interactions for repeated-conversation patterns
- network egress and TLS termination for private deployments

Attached is the runtime spec we've been using (bf_runtime_spec.pdf). Can your team run a focused technical validation and produce: a test matrix, a short runbook for any configuration pins, and a list of failing edge-cases (if any)?

Desired timeline: validation window Oct 25–27, with a short readout the week after. Please include Synture's point person on the thread — Tom Harris (cc'd separately).

Thanks,
– Anika Rao
Director, Strategic Integrations
BeaconForge

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@beaconforge.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@synture.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BeaconForge / Synture — initial validation scope and runtime spec

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear scope and the spec.

We can run the validation window you proposed. Quick asks before we finalize the plan:

1) Tom / Synture: can you share the architecture diagram that shows where the connector sits (sidecar vs. proxy) and whether calls will be to hosted API endpoints or a Private VPC endpoint during the test window?
2) Marissa (Solutions): please confirm the baseline model variants we should use (open model + quantized variant?) and the latency SLOs we should test for.
3) Legal / Ops: we need the signed test-data agreement (DocuSign link) for the sample corpus if it contains PII.

I'll pull together the Redwood checklist and a first-pass test matrix. Tentative meeting to review the matrix: Tue Oct 19, 09:30 PT. If that works for everyone, I'll send an invite.

Attachments: none

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anika Rao <anika.rao@beaconforge.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@synture.io>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BeaconForge / Synture — initial validation scope and runtime spec

Thanks Vivek / Anika. I've drafted a preliminary assessment and the items we need to validate. Summary below and I've attached the partner checklist (redwood-partner-checklist.xlsx).

Quick summary / risk areas:
- Model variants & quantization: we need explicit model IDs for hosted vs private (e.g., redwood-open-1.1 / redwood-open-1.1-q4). Without exact pins, parity checks will be noisy.
- Streaming + KV-cache: repeated conversation scenarios can expose inconsistent cache hits across different backend pools; we should include deterministic prompt prefixes to detect cache divergence.
- Tokenization edge cases: non-UTF8 byte sequences and extraordinary long tokens (>= 32k chars) have produced encoding errors in prior integrations. Add input fuzzing.
- Network & auth: for Private tests, we need a small terraform snippet or a manifest that shows allowed egress ranges so our egress smoke tests can be executed.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
1) Baseline parity: 1000 synthetic prompts, compare outputs using normalized metrics (ROUGE/EM)
2) Latency tails: 5k requests with bursty distribution (95/99/99.9 percentile)
3) Edge-case fuzzing: 1k mutated inputs covering emoji, combined scripts, and corrupted UTF-8
4) Streaming correctness: 200 multi-token streams with intentional mid-stream reconnects
5) Egress validation: outbound IPs, DNS behavior, TLS cert validation

Please confirm the model pins and whether BeaconForge will run a lightweight pre-check on their side to confirm request signing.

Attachments:
- redwood-partner-checklist.xlsx (partner validation checklist, test cases, and pass/fail criteria)

I'll join the Tue meeting and bring a short runbook draft.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anika Rao <anika.rao@beaconforge.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@synture.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BeaconForge / Synture — initial validation scope and runtime spec

Adding a few operational items from Redwood Dedicated / Private playbooks:

- Egress smoke script: I'll attach a small script (egress-test-plan.sh) that checks outbound IPs, TLS chains, and response times against known endpoints. BeaconForge / Synture should run it from their environment and provide results.
- Canary policy: during the validation window we'll run canary traffic at 10% of total traffic to avoid wide blast radius. Confirm if BeaconForge needs any special routing (e.g., path-based routing to a canary pool).
- Observable hooks: add a token-level header in test requests (x-rw-test-id) so we can correlate traces and measure per-route latency.
- Failure modes: if streaming errors exceed 1% we automatically scale to a fallback model for continued availability; Will BeaconForge accept that fallback behavior for the test window?

Attachments:
- egress-test-plan.sh (script stub)

I'll be on the call Tue morning to walk through the observability hooks and canary steps.

—Sergio
Partner Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Harris <tharris@synture.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@beaconforge.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BeaconForge / Synture — initial validation scope and runtime spec

Thanks all — this looks good and aligned. A few quick confirmations:

- Architecture: BeaconForge connector will run as an outbound sidecar in the customer pod and call Redwood Private (VPC) during the test window. We'll provide the VPC CIDR & egress ranges by EOD tomorrow.
- Model pins: Synture will request redwood-open-1.1 on hosted and redwood-open-1.1-q4 on private for parity testing.
- Data & agreements: Anika has started the DocuSign via the link you have in the thread; Synture will only load synthetic samples derived from production. We will upload the corpus to S3 here: s3://beaconforge-test-data/edgecases.zip and provide presigned URLs.
- Test window: we confirm Oct 25–27. We accept the canary fallback policy for availability.

Links:
- S3 test corpus (private presigned will be shared in the doc): s3://beaconforge-test-data/edgecases.zip
- DocuSign (test-data NDA): https://www.docusign.com/instance/EnvelopeID_7a2b9c

We'll be ready to run the pre-checks on Oct 22 and hand over the canary routing manifest by Oct 23. Looking forward to the readout.

Cheers,
Tom Harris
Integration Lead, Synture
